problem: Peripheral areas of the city rely on private water tankers with little price transparency or quality assurance, making it hard for residents to compare vendors or raise complaints.
project_idea: A web or WhatsApp-based aggregator for registered water tanker vendors, letting residents compare rates and report quality issues to the relevant civic authority.

problem: Urban households have limited awareness of authorised e-waste collection points. Informal collectors often handle e-waste without safety measures.
project_idea: A map of authorised e-waste collection points maintained by the state pollution control authority, with a simple booking flow for household drop-offs.

problem: Low-lying neighbourhoods experience recurrent waterlogging during the northeast monsoon, and early warnings do not reliably reach residents in local languages.
project_idea: A Tamil-language flood alert bot (Telegram or WhatsApp) ingesting publicly available rainfall data from the national weather agency and sending ward-level warnings ahead of expected flooding.

problem: Patients at government hospitals spend considerable time waiting for OPD tokens with no prior visibility into department load, leading to avoidable travel during high-demand periods.
project_idea: A live queue display (web dashboard or in-hospital screen) showing OPD load by department, so patients can check before travelling.

problem: The official air quality monitoring network has limited coverage in older city areas and near industrial zones, leaving residents without hyperlocal pollution data.
project_idea: A low-cost PM2.5 sensor network deployed at schools and community centres, with a live map shared with the state pollution control authority.

problem: Wet and dry waste segregation compliance varies across city wards, and civic supervisors lack a real-time view of which areas need follow-up.
project_idea: A mobile app for waste collection staff to log segregation status per stop, with a ward-level compliance heatmap for supervisors.
